note: What tools/harvest_flickr.py is to fetch, and where each photograph goes. One entry per record per photograph; a photograph wanted by two records is listed twice and each record gets its own copy and its own alt text. The harvester re-reads every page's rights before it downloads, so a licence that changes here is caught there. Alt text is written by hand from looking at the picture, not copied from the archive's caption.

items.author: Bill Sharpe; State Archives of North Carolina
items.credit: Department of Conservation and Development, Travel Information Division Photograph Collection, State Archives of North Carolina
items.alt: A News Bureau photo sheet: two prints mounted on a printed North Carolina Department of Conservation and Development form, filled in by hand — subject, Barbeque Pit; locality, Goldsboro, Adam Scotts Place; date, Aug-44. In the left print a man in a white shirt and apron stands at a table with two tall enamel stockpots and an open pan of chopped meat, a short-handled tool in his raised hand and printed notices tacked to the board wall behind him. The right print looks down the inside of a long brick pit: a bed of pale ash between low brick walls, iron bars laid across it, the far end lost in smoke.

items.author: Bill Sharpe; State Archives of North Carolina
items.credit: Department of Conservation and Development, Travel Information Division Photograph Collection, State Archives of North Carolina
items.alt: A state News Bureau photo sheet headed Barbeque Pit, locality Goldsboro, Adam Scotts Place, dated Aug-44 in pencil. Two prints are mounted on it. One shows a man in a white shirt and apron at a table with two tall enamel stockpots and a pan of chopped meat, working with a short-handled tool; notices are tacked to the plank wall behind him. The other looks along the inside of a long brick pit, ash on the floor between brick walls and iron bars laid across.

items.author: Bill Sharpe; State Archives of North Carolina
items.credit: Department of Conservation and Development, Travel Information Division Photograph Collection, State Archives of North Carolina
items.alt: The right-hand print on a 1944 state News Bureau sheet looks straight down the inside of a masonry barbecue pit at Goldsboro: a low wall of brick on each side, a floor of pale ash and charred wood between them, iron bars laid across the opening, and the far end of the chamber dark with smoke. The sheet's handwritten caption reads Barbeque Pit, Goldsboro, Adam Scotts Place, Aug-44.

items.author: State Archives of North Carolina
items.credit: PhC.184 Massengill Postcard Collection, State Archives of North Carolina
items.alt: A colour-tinted postcard of a long low white building with a small columned porch at the centre, seen across a bare sand lot with eight or nine cars of the 1940s parked nose-in. A steel post at the left carries a sign in two panels: PARKERS BAR-B-Q over STEAKS CHICKEN, with a smaller board beneath reading OYSTER BAR. Pines and open field run along behind the roofline.

items.author: State Archives of North Carolina
items.credit: FCX Photograph Collection, PhC.23, State Archives of North Carolina
items.alt: A black-and-white photograph taken from across a downtown street. A two-storey brick building holds the corner; over its ground-floor windows a painted fascia reads COOPER'S, AIR CONDITIONED, and a second awning beside it reads BARBECUE, AIR CONDITIONED, with a hanging bracket sign between them repeating Cooper's Barbecue. Two women walk past the door carrying bags, a long sedan is parked at the kerb and a bus stands in the alley beyond. NO SIGNS is painted on a wall at the left edge.

items.author: State Archives of North Carolina
items.credit: PhC.184 Massengill Postcard Collection, State Archives of North Carolina
items.alt: A colour postcard of a meal laid on a red-and-white checked tablecloth, the words WILBER'S BARBECUE across the top in gold. On the large plate, a mound of chopped pork, a scoop of pale slaw, french fries and a piece of chicken under gravy. Beside it a side plate of hushpuppies, a tall glass of iced tea with a lemon wedge, a bottle of Wilber's barbecue sauce with a pig on the label, and a knife, fork and spoon laid on a red napkin.

items.author: State Archives of North Carolina
items.credit: PhC.184 Massengill Postcard Collection, State Archives of North Carolina
items.alt: A colour postcard divided into three panels. Across the top, a long flat-roofed brick and stucco restaurant with BARBECUE LODGE in raised letters over the entrance and cars and pickups of the late 1970s parked in front. Lower left, a smaller shingled building with a steep roof on a street corner. Lower right, a low white building whose sign reads BARBECUE LODGE TAKE OUT SERVICE, with trucks at the kerb and a petrol pump beside the door.

items.author: State Archives of North Carolina
items.credit: PhC.184 Massengill Postcard Collection, State Archives of North Carolina
items.alt: A colour-tinted linen postcard of a long low white restaurant with a columned centre porch, across a bare sand lot holding eight or nine parked cars of the 1940s. A steel post at the left carries PARKERS BAR-B-Q over STEAKS CHICKEN, and a smaller board below reads OYSTER BAR. The sky is tinted a flat blue and the lot a flat cream.

items.author: Albert Barden; State Archives of North Carolina
items.credit: Albert Barden Collection, State Archives of North Carolina
items.alt: A man in a straw hat, white shirt and braces bends over a shallow trench dug in bare ground. Green poles are laid across the trench as a grate and meat lies on them, smoke rising through. He holds a small tin pail low in his right hand and reaches into the meat with his left. A barefoot boy in a light suit stands at one side of the clearing and a girl in a checked dress and wide hat at the other, both watching. Felled logs and woods behind.

items.author: John Hemmer; State Archives of North Carolina
items.credit: Department of Conservation and Development, Travel Information Division Photograph Collection, State Archives of North Carolina
items.alt: A state News Bureau sheet of four prints headed Barbeque, Braswell Plantation, Sept 1944. Two of them show a man in a cap and overalls standing over a long open trench beside a cinder-block building: split hogs lie flat on close-laid poles across the trench, and he leans out over them with a pan in one hand and a long-handled mop in the other. A third print shows two men at a wooden trough, one bringing a cleaver down on a heap of cooked pork while the other steadies it, with a bushel tub of chopped meat below. The fourth shows mule wagons full of people coming up a sand road between pines.

items.author: John Hemmer; State Archives of North Carolina
items.credit: Department of Conservation and Development, Travel Information Division Photograph Collection, State Archives of North Carolina
items.alt: A state News Bureau sheet of four prints headed Barbeque, Braswell Plantation, Sept 1944. In the top right print two pairs of hands work over a wooden trough: one brings a cleaver down through a pile of cooked pork, another rakes the chopped meat towards a wooden bushel tub already heaped full. The other prints show a plank table running away down a slope set with dozens of loaded plates, a man stirring a black iron cauldron over a wood fire under a shed roof, and a man in overalls basting meat laid on poles over an open trench.

items.author: John Hemmer; State Archives of North Carolina
items.credit: Department of Conservation and Development, Travel Information Division Photograph Collection, State Archives of North Carolina
items.alt: A state News Bureau sheet of four prints headed Barbeque, Braswell Plantation, Sept 1944. In the bottom right print three black iron cauldrons stand on stones over open wood fires under a shed roof, steam pouring off all three, with mule wagons and a field behind. The other prints show a plank table lined with jars of preserves and a string band playing from the bed of a truck, wagons parked among the pines with children running between them, and three men in hats peeling and cutting vegetables into galvanised washtubs.

items.author: John Hemmer; State Archives of North Carolina
items.credit: Department of Conservation and Development, Travel Information Division Photograph Collection, State Archives of North Carolina
items.alt: In the top right print of a 1944 state News Bureau sheet from a barbecue at Braswell Plantation, three men in hats and shirtsleeves stand at a trestle table peeling and cutting vegetables. A galvanised washtub heaped with whole potatoes sits between them, a second tub holds the cut pieces under water, and two more buckets and a tub wait on the table. A fourth man works at a bench behind, and a long plank counter runs off to a fence and an open field.

items.author: John Hemmer; State Archives of North Carolina
items.credit: Department of Conservation and Development, Travel Information Division Photograph Collection, State Archives of North Carolina
items.alt: A state News Bureau sheet of four prints headed Barbeque, Braswell Plantation near Rocky Mount, Sept 1944. One shows a crowd standing among tall pines with plates in their hands, children in front, wagons and mules at the treeline. One shows a queue several hundred people long curving away under the trees. One looks down on servers working a line of trestle tables spread with large pans, people filing past with plates. The fourth is close: a woman and three small children sitting on the grass, plates of food and a cup set out on the ground beside them, the smallest child in a white sun hat eating with her fingers.

items.author: John Hemmer; State Archives of North Carolina
items.credit: Department of Conservation and Development, Travel Information Division Photograph Collection, State Archives of North Carolina
items.alt: A state News Bureau sheet of four prints headed Barbeque, Braswell Plantation, Sept 1944. In one, several hundred people sit on plank benches among pines facing a low wooden platform where a man in shirtsleeves stands at the front and others sit in chairs behind him. Another looks the same crowd in the face, rows deep, cars parked in the trees behind. A third shows two mule wagons carrying people along a sand road. The fourth shows people sitting on the grass with plates, a man in overalls walking towards the camera carrying his.

items.author: H. H. Brimley; State Archives of North Carolina
items.credit: H. H. Brimley Collection, PhC.42, State Archives of North Carolina
items.alt: A dark, rough-coated hog stands alone on flat sandy ground with its snout down, rooting. The ground is bare but for tufts of coarse grass. On the horizon behind it are a shingled barn with a lean-to, a line of low scrub, and a beached hull lying on its side.

items.author: H. H. Brimley; State Archives of North Carolina
items.credit: H. H. Brimley Collection, PhC.42, State Archives of North Carolina
items.alt: A lean black hog with a ridge of bristles standing up along its back walks across open white sand, snout lowered, its own tracks running away behind it. The beach and the sky beyond are blank and almost the same tone, with a faint line of surf at the right.

items.author: State Archives of North Carolina
items.credit: Department of Conservation and Development, Travel and Tourism photo files, State Archives of North Carolina
items.alt: A barefoot man in a felt hat and bib overalls walks up a sandy row between two head-high rows of tobacco, a bundle of broad cropped leaves gripped under each arm. The plants on the right have flowered at the top. The soil of the row is pale sand, printed with bare footprints.
